$comment: Single source of truth for the core<->shell contract. Both languages are GENERATED from this file; neither is written by hand. See the protocol spec §2.4 and §2.5.
$privileged: A command that carries Bytes or mutates the filesystem must be `privileged: true` (§2.4, §24.8). A Bytes value comes from a native dialog owned by the shell; the renderer may never originate a path or an executable and must never call one of these directly.
$mutatesFilesystem: A command that mutates the filesystem is `privileged: true` (§24.8), so `isRendererCallable` refuses it on `IPC_REQUEST` and it travels a shell-owned channel.
$idempotent: `idempotent: false` marks the operations §2.2 forbids auto-replaying: a launch, a session mutation, a flag change. On core death these are rejected with `outcome: "unknown"` and surfaced to the user.

ProblemKind.$comment: §11.1's groups. `abandoned_install` is the ninth and, like `deferred_slow` and `ambiguous_lineage`, is NOT a `ScanProblemKind`: it reads `install_run`, never `scan_problem`, so that table's CHECK constraint and `problem_kind_from_storage` are both untouched and no migration is involved (R26).

SortKey.$comment: [p3] §35.2's fourth key. **The array's order is the control's cycle order**, so a new key joins last, after the three that shipped. `needs_attention` orders on `HealthSummary.scoredOpen` descending and tails every row carrying no reading; it is an item count and never a score, and it is offered only when a row in the projection carries one (§35.5). `completion` is still absent and is §31's to move.

ViewState.$comment: §8: `savedAt` is null on a fresh install and non-null on a restored view, which is the only thing separating the two — every other field reads identically when a client deliberately saves an empty shelf, so without it a first run and a cleared shelf are indistinguishable on the wire. It is deliberately NOT on ViewPatch: the core stamps it inside view.set, so a client cannot forge a provenance it does not have

RemoteLinkKind.$comment: §25.2: the five links out of the REMOTE tab. The renderer names a kind and never a URL; the core builds the string from this project's own remote_key against the host allowlist.

BackupState.$comment: §25.3's backup state, as a DECISION and never as copy. Three variants, not four: the fourth row of the table is the absent field, and an absent field plus a variant meaning nothing would be one value stated twice. Per §19.4 phase 2 has no push, so this states a fact and offers no control.

RemoteFactsState.$comment: §25.1's four states of a forge-derived value. Staleness is NOT one of them: it is now minus observedAt past a threshold, and therefore a function of the moment it is rendered.

RemoteVisibility.$comment: §25.3: both render or neither does. Rendering only `private` makes its absence assert public, which is the invented fact §8.5.1 cut the field for.

CiRun.$comment: §25.4: `conclusion` is a nullable String and NOT an enum. The vocabulary belongs to the forge, and a closed mirror of a third party's vocabulary is R26 by construction. NULL means the run had not concluded when it was observed.

CiList.$comment: §25.7: its own state and its own clock. The Actions read and the repo-facts read are two reads, and a CI list dated by the other one is the staleness marker lying.

RemoteFacts.$comment: §25.1. `key` is the project's remote_key, carried for rendering only; the wire shape names no provider_repo_id, which is §22's binding and not a fact. `linkable` is the core's answer to whether this key produces a link, so the renderer holds no second copy of the host allowlist.

ReadmeSource.$comment: [p2] §25.5: the document projects.readme reads, as against ReadmeState's stored first paragraph. `path` is which of README_NAMES matched, so the panel's header names the file it actually read. `truncated` is a stated fact, never an implication that the document ended.

ClosedBy.$comment: §9: a segment closes for a narrower set of reasons than a session does. 'stop', 'process_exit' and 'orphaned' end a session; the segment open at that moment closes as 'session_end'. Not a duplicate of CloseReason — do not collapse them

UninstallDisposition.$comment: §24.8. `unknown` is distinct from `blocked` at the TYPE level, not by convention: collapsing them would render an absence as a fact, and neither disposition reaches removal anyway.

UninstallBlocker.$comment: §24.8: the verdict is never a boolean. Every failing condition is named so a surface states WHY a control is disabled rather than only disabling it. Ten are known-bad; four — shallow_clone, remote_unreachable, stash_unreadable, never_observed — are unknowns.

UninstallVerdict.$comment: §24.8's per-item value. `blockers` always carries EVERY blocker found, of both classes, so the fold never hides one. No token crosses this boundary: the seal `locations.uninstall` compares against is in-core only.

DebtSource.$comment: [p3] §28.2's nine sources, closed (A4). The `debt_item.source` CHECK in `0013_debt.sql` mirrors this list character for character (R26). Five further sources are declared in §28's prose and are deliberately in neither place — `forge_issues`, `lint_warnings`, `compiler_warnings`, `failing_tests`, `stale_merged_branches`; a tenth costs one migration plus one regenerate. No variant may take one of the four names §30.6 rules out; the ban is enforced by check-forbidden:p3-28-debt-source-names (AC-P3-28-18a) rather than restated here.

DebtItemState.$comment: [p3] §28.3's two stored states. *Closed* is an EVENT and never a state: the row is deleted and the `xp_events` ledger is the permanent record. There is no third stored state and no user-facing dismissal.

DebtScoring.$comment: [p3] §28's A7 property, orthogonal to the item's state. A `shown_only` item renders and lights its layer (§33) and is excluded from the health count (§30), from §35's sort and from any XP payout. The two states are about OBSERVATION; this is about CONSEQUENCE — folding them puts six meanings in one column.

DebtSweepOutcome.$comment: [p3] §28.5's six outcomes. Four of them are reasons the sweep could not finish, which is why the outcome is an explicit stored value and never row-presence: presence carries one bit. `skipped_suppressed` is unreachable until p3-30 replaces §29's `compute_suppressed`.

ObservationBasis.$comment: [p3] §28.5's five bases. A worktree-basis observation and a HEAD-basis observation are not comparable and may not be diffed for a closure (A9). `index` is declared although no phase-3 source produces it — §29's content scan reads the index and §28 must be able to say so.

DecayLayer.$comment: [p3] Declared by §28 because `DebtItem.layer` is the first field that needs it and §28 lands a wave earlier; **§33 owns every rule over it** and declares it nowhere (R113, A14.1, R31). The ORDER is the total order A3's tie-break needs and is not alphabetical.

Ecosystem.$comment: [p3] §32.5. The set is a property of THIS APP'S PARSER COVERAGE, not of the source's vocabulary: an ecosystem is listed once a lockfile of its shape can be read. Every slug is character-identical to the endpoint's own `ecosystem` parameter because it is sent as one. 0014_advisories.sql's ecosystem CHECKs are written from these slugs character for character (R26).

DependencyReadState.$comment: [p3] §32.6's two READ outcomes, and deliberately not three: *the scan has not run* is the ABSENCE of a `project_dependency_scan` row, not a third variant, because a file that was not read produces no (package, version) key to carry one. A cap exceedance is `notRead`, never a partial parse — a short triple set produces a false clean. `project_lockfile.read_state`'s CHECK is written from these slugs.

DependencyVerdict.$comment: [p3] §32.8, derived at read time from two clocks and stored nowhere. **These are not §30's four pipeline states** and are never folded into them: a project can be live and `unknown` at once, and one vocabulary makes that state unsayable. `unknown` is never rendered as zero and never as a dark tick — it leaves the reading's numerator AND denominator. R130/F9: §30.4's ban on the word `clean` is scoped to RENDERINGS, and this wire value is never rendered as that word.

AdvisoryDetail.$comment: [p3] R118: **one nullable struct on DebtItem, not six nullable fields NULL for eight of the nine sources.** `severity` is the source's own vocabulary stored verbatim and carries no CHECK and no enum — a closed mirror of a third party's vocabulary is R26 by construction, already ruled for `CiRunPayload.conclusion` (core/src/provider/mod.rs:192-194). `cveIds` is a LIST because one GHSA carries several CVE ids or none: unreviewed and malware advisories have none.

AdvisoryAlert.$comment: [p3] §32.12's payload, one settle away from the one OS notification phase 3 may fire. **The five nullable fields are Some only when exactly one project and one advisory fired.** No field may express an absence: no excluded count, no suppressed count, no reason — §11.3a's footer states that no notification mentions absence, and a field naming one breaches the ceiling by addition rather than by wording. `cveId` is nullable because the notifiable unit is the ADVISORY: a critical advisory with no CVE id is still notifiable, and the copy says *advisory* when there is no id to name.

DebtItem.$comment: [p3] §28.9's item. Identity is `(subject_key, source, fingerprint)` and is not on the wire; `pathDisplay`, `line`, `column` and `salientText` are ATTRIBUTES, so a rename closes nothing and a line move closes nothing. `state` crosses the wire so the list can say *this item is not being counted right now*; `unverified` is never a count on a ranked or aggregated surface (R128/F10).

DebtSweepState.$comment: [p3] §28.5's sweep, on the wire. Without it, zero items means both *no debt* and *nobody looked*. `itemCount` is nullable for the same reason its column is: `AC-P3-28-11` requires *not computed* and *zero* to differ on the wire and not only in the store. A source with no row was never observed.

Rect.$comment: [p3] §33.3's anchor rectangle in §7.3's 2x card space: top-left origin, y down, `i32` exactly as `core/src/art/scene.rs` stores it. R115: the section wrote `[[i32]]` and the grammar parses only `Name` | `Name?` | `[Name]` | `[Name]?`, so `validateSchema` throws before `gen` emits — a named struct is what the grammar's own docstring prescribes, and it is also what makes the shape greppable from the spec.

Point.$comment: [p3] §33.3's rust anchor: the fastener centre alone. **No `kind` and no `rot`** — the head is in the bitmap and the layer draws only the stain, which runs +y under gravity and does not read the head's orientation. Two fields nothing would read are two fields that drift.

Polyline.$comment: [p3] §33.3's cracks anchor: one seam path. A struct rather than `[[i32]]` for R115's reason, and a struct rather than `[Point]` directly because `WeatherLayer.paths` is a list OF polylines and the grammar does not nest.

WeatherLayer.$comment: [p3] §33.3's resolved anchors for one layer. **Three typed arrays rather than one tagged list**: each layer's anchor kind is fixed by the table, so a tag would be a second spelling of `layer`. **AT MOST ONE is non-empty (R127.1)** — on a `Plain` scene with no vents, the majority shape, `dust` and `overgrowth` resolve to zero anchors and all three are empty. `layer` references p3-28's generated enum and re-declares nothing (R113, R31).

Weathering.$comment: [p3] §33.8's reply. It carries geometry and **nothing about debt**: no value, no item id, no `computedAt` and no freeze state — the anchor set is a pure function of the stored scene document, and the lit set is the renderer's. `sceneHash` is NULL when the project has no `art_scene` row, and `layers` is then empty. `spaceW`/`spaceH` are `u32` while the stored space is `i32`; the handler casts once at the reply and REFUSES rather than truncating a negative, because a silent `as u32` turns a corrupt document into an enormous positive.

ProjectDetail.$comment: [p3] `conditionMaterial` is §33.7's inner needle — the COMMIT clock, beside `row.conditionSignal`'s interaction clock. R138: phase 1 computes and stores it (`core/src/derive/persist.rs:26,142,158`) and it reached no wire type at all, which made `AC-P3-33-11` unpassable. It reuses the generated `ConditionSignal` and declares no second enum (R31), so it is a FIELD addition and moves no total. **NULL means *never computed*** and draws no inner needle and no divergence line — never a needle at zero. It lands on `ProjectDetail` rather than `ProjectRow` because the panel is page-only, the same shape as §30.7's *no grid surface renders a health count*. `completion` is §31.6's, NULL until ten rows exist.

HealthState.$comment: [p3] §30.1's four states, IN PRECEDENCE ORDER — `absent` > `suppressed` > `frozen` > `live`. Each gate answers a question that makes the next meaningless if answered the other way, so a reordering is a behaviour change. It says which reading a surface is looking at; it is NOT a flag a consumer branches on, and §33 and §35 re-derive none of it.

CheckOutcome.$comment: [p3] §30.3's five outcomes. `ran = ok + failed` is the only denominator this system has, and a check enters it only by producing one of those two — which is what makes it impossible to report a suppressed, switched-off or failed check as a passing one. `off` and `notApplicable` are disjoint fields and no arithmetic path moves a value into `ran`.

ProjectLifecycle.$comment: [p3] §30.8's tri-state, computed once beside the debt list and expressed nowhere else. **NOT a variant added to `ConditionSignal`**: that column is `Option<ConditionSignal>` over seven ACTIVITY bands, and `done` is a lifecycle verdict — putting it there adds a meaningless variant to `condition_signal`, which shares the enum.

UnknownReason.$comment: [p3] §30.3's six reasons. An `unknown` check is counted AND named: the reason is never omitted, defaulted or collapsed to one string. `notRunYet` and `unreachable` are `notObserved`'s two self-resolving neighbours and are separate from it deliberately — a user owed a different act is owed a different sentence. `notSynced` is *the value has not been read back from its source*; §32.4's provider method takes no token, so it never asserts an account (R131/F7). An ungranted content scan is `off`, never a seventh variant here (R128/F8).

HealthBasis.$comment: [p3] §30.3's per-check basis. **Checks only — it holds no item count** (A12b): a struct carrying one VALUE over two units is the violation, and a basis carrying items is how that arrives. `observedAt` is the OLDEST input, not the newest: a reading is only as current as its stalest input, and dating it by the freshest read is the staleness marker lying.

HealthCheck.$comment: [p3] §30.3's per-check row. **A health check is a debt source (A17)**, never one of §31's ten completion checks — §30 mirrors neither the registry's membership nor its size, and no number for it appears in any type here. `unknownReason` is present exactly when `outcome` is `unknown`.

HealthReading.$comment: [p3] §30.1's reading, on the project page. `scoredOpen` and `basis` are NULL with **no default** and the writer is forbidden to write `0` for unknown — `completion_lit`'s enforcement shape (§1.10), core-side and unit-tested. `checks` is empty for `absent` and `suppressed`, and an empty array is the state saying nothing was computed, never a count of zero checks.

HealthSummary.$comment: [p3] §30.11's shelf flattening of the reading, nullable **exactly where `HealthReading` is, field for field** (R116, correcting A14.3's shape). `unverified` is the one quantity the reading does not carry — the page reads it off `ProjectDetail.debt`, and the shelf has no items, which is why R117 puts the count here and deletes `DebtCounts`. `scoredOpen` counts ITEMS and `unknownChecks` counts CHECKS: two units, named, never combined.

HealthCheckSwitch.$comment: [p3] §30.9's switch, GLOBAL — one row per check in §11.3a's drawer. Per-project *not-applicable* is a different statement and reuses §31's archetype-proposed mechanism. Off HIDES; it never closes an item and never pays: a switch that closed items would make turning a check off an XP source. The core emits one entry per `DebtSource` variant, always in full.

CompletionCheck.$comment: [p3] §31.1a's ten keys, verbatim. Declared once here and hand-written on neither side (R31); `project_check.check_key`'s CHECK in `0015_completion.sql` is written from these slugs character for character. The spelling is in BIJECTION with `DebtSource`, never identity — `readme` stands behind `missing_readme` — and §31.9 forbids conflating the two.

CheckState.$comment: [p3] §31.1's four states. **The spellings differ from `CheckOutcome`'s on purpose; a shared spelling invites the join A17 forbids** — health's set is A4's nine-source registry and completion's is these ten keys, and the two are never summed, joined or rendered as one list. `unknown` is never `fail`, never `0` and never absent (R128/F14).

CompletionCheckRow.$comment: [p3] §31.5's stored row, on the wire. `unknownReason` is present exactly when `state` is `unknown`, and its variants are §30's — referenced, never declared here (R31). **No `basis` field**: the basis is a property of the check KEY, constant per key, and is stated in §31.1a's table rather than stored per row (A9). `observedAt` is when the state was last ESTABLISHED, not when it was last attempted.

CompletionDetail.$comment: [p3] §31.6's detail. Non-NULL **iff ten rows exist**, so the `evaluable == 0` case carries `lit: 0, evaluable: 0` and all ten rows with their reasons — the only surface that says why nothing could be scored. **No rendered figure is ever decided from these scalars**: the frame, the list score and the hero band read `ProjectRow.completionLit` / `completionApplicable`, which is the NULL. The three counts are recountable from `checks` and `AC-P3-31-1` recounts them.

Peek.$comment: [p2] §25.3a: `remote` is NULL iff project.remote_key is NULL, the same predicate ProjectDetail.remote carries. Peek draws §25.1's blocks at Peek's size from the same producer; it is not a second place they are computed.

Rendition.$comment: R47: two blueprint variants, not one. §7.6 addresses a rendition as codotheca://art/<hash>/<rendition>, so one variant cannot address two render passes — a cached raster of one would be served for the other at exactly the moment the project changes state.

ReadmeAssetState.$comment: [p2] §25.5: `blocked` is the CONSENT state and is never rendered as a failure. The other four are outcomes of a read that was allowed to happen.

ReadmeAsset.$comment: [p2] §25.5: `ref` is the reference verbatim as it appeared in the document, so the renderer can put the bytes back on the node it took it from. `dataUri` is present only for `ok`, and `fetchedAt` dates a read that happened — a blocked asset observed nothing.

ReadmeRemoteChanged.$comment: [p2] §25.5: `allowedAt` NULL is never granted, a timestamp is granted at T. The event carries the value rather than a boolean so the renderer's optimistic flip and the wire cannot disagree — the ProjectFlagsChanged precedent.

ConnectStage.$comment: R78: not_stored is terminal and is neither denied nor expired. denied is the user refusing at the forge and expired is the deadline elapsing; a code that was redeemed and whose grant this machine could not store is a third thing, and reporting it as either of the other two is a false statement about what happened.

Account.$comment: §20.8: carries no token field at any nesting depth. The database stores token_ref and the keychain stores the secret; the renderer holds neither.

ConnectProgress.$comment: R78: reason is non-null for exactly one stage, not_stored — which of the forge and this machine refused is the whole of what the user is owed there. Every other stage carries null.

InstallStageKind.$comment: §24.4's phases. `settled` is terminal and is reported like any other, so a readout never has to infer the end from silence.

InstallRefusal.$comment: §24.3d. A refusal is a REPLY, not an error frame: every failing condition is named so a surface can state why, and a `-2` suffix is never generated to make one go away.

InstallFailure.$comment: §24: how a run that started ends badly. Distinct from InstallRefusal, which is why one never began — a refusal costs nothing and a failure may have left a staging directory behind.

InstallDestination.$comment: §24.3a: the renderer names a destination by RootId and the core composes the rest, so the renderer never builds a path. `display` is §1.10's lossy display form and is never used to open, launch or compare; `rootId` with `seedBasename` is the identity the core re-derives the real path from.

InstallPreview.$comment: §24.3d: the composed display form and the collision verdict together, on CollectionUpsert's shape. Folding the refusal into the display string is how a refusal stops being a reply.

InstallStart.$comment: §24.8: the verdict is recomputed inside the mutating call and the start refuses if it changed, so this answers with a run id or with the reason there is none. A verdict rendered thirty seconds ago is a cache.

InstallStage.$comment: A10: `done` and `total` are per-phase and both nullable, and there is NO aggregate field by construction — so no surface can render the retreating percentage §10.2 bans. Do not add one.

InstallState.$comment: R54: every running and recently-settled run, so a renderer that opens mid-clone builds a frame from a snapshot rather than from the next event to arrive. `started` is why this is two lists and not one: InstallStage carries no projectId and its field set is pinned so no aggregate can be added, so `runs` alone cannot tell a tile which run is its own — which is the case the snapshot exists for. It brings the composed display form with it, which a tile mounting mid-clone needs anyway. One entry per run in each list, joined on runId.

InstallFailed.$comment: §24: `detail` is the sentence a surface may show beside the named reason, never in place of it — the enum is what a surface branches on.

SyncTaskKind.$comment: §21.3's task vocabulary. R31: declared here and used generated on both sides. [p3] 0014_advisories.sql's task CHECK is written from these slugs character for character, and a test inserts every one against a migrated database rather than restating the list. **The tally this comment used to carry is removed rather than incremented** — §36.2 rule 9, a count a human maintains is a defect with a delay; the variants below are the count. [p3] `advisories` is the first process-wide task and the first that runs unauthenticated: its row carries key IS NULL and occupies the sync_task_global slot

SyncTaskState.$comment: §21.4's state table. deferred and blocked are both terminal to the clock and differ in what revives them: deferred takes a revival cause, blocked takes an account state change or an explicit user action and is never left on a backoff

SyncOutcomeKind.$comment: §21.9's closed outcome enum, flattened: the wire carries which outcome it was and none of its data. The Rust SyncOutcome::Throttled additionally carries whether the limit was secondary, because §21.4 backs the two off differently and the headers are gone by then — that is a Rust widening and not a wire one, so this list is §21.13's exactly

SyncNotice.$comment: §21.10's four sentences. Sync failure is state, not a command error: no ErrorCode is declared, because the closed enum describes a command failing while background sync failure lives on the sync rows and this topic

SyncListingSummary.$comment: §21.10's settle-time count set. suppressedBy is R62's: §22.6 requires a suppression be reported with the project that blocked it named, and a count cannot name one. It is positionally aligned with the suppressions and NOT deduplicated, so suppressedBy.length == suppressed is an invariant; an empty list means nothing was suppressed and never not computed, which is why the count stays beside it

SyncTaskSettled.$comment: state is carried rather than re-derived: §21.8's outcome-to-state mapping is not total, because TransientFail becomes queued or deferred depending on a fail_count no event carries. outcome is nullable because it is NOT OBSERVED HERE in two different ways: a queued row has never produced one, and sync.status reports the stored row, which carries a state and not an outcome — sync_task_state has no column for one. The settled event is where an observed outcome travels. null is therefore *no outcome is being reported*, and a surface must not render it as *never settled*

SyncBudget.$comment: accountId is nullable because NULL is the unauthenticated per-IP pool, keyed by the absence of an account rather than by a sentinel one. Every number is nullable for the same reason it is nullable in the table: unobserved is unknown, never zero and never the limit

SyncListingProgress.$comment: §21.11: total is nullable because a denominator inferred from page numbers is a guess, and a guessed denominator is an unknown rendered as a fact. listed only ever increases

SyncStatus.$comment: sync.status' answer and the sync topic's snapshot, byte for byte the same value

commands.name: roots.list
commands.$comment: §11.3a draws a row per root and an `N OF M ACTIVE` caption; §2.4's table declared only the mutations, so nothing returned the set. Read-only and unprivileged: no path crosses in either direction, only RootId and path_display. Plan 16 implements the handler

commands.name: roots.add
commands.$comment: privileged: the path originates from a shell-owned native dialog, never from the renderer. §10.1a's refuse-list answers with RootRefusal and an explanation, never a silent no

commands.name: projects.list
commands.$comment: §8.2: every field is optional with a stated default, because the projects topic's snapshot calls this with {}. `window` is the same shape the response carries, so a caller pages by echoing back the window it was given rather than by rebuilding from/to

commands.name: projects.readme
commands.$comment: §25.5: the whole document under J6_BYTE_CAP, which this command reads from the existing constant rather than declaring a second cap. ReadmeState.text is first_paragraph's output and is a different value with a different job

commands.name: projects.readmeAssets
commands.$comment: §25.5: the bytes behind a README's images, as data: URIs the core produced. The two arrays are the renderer's split on ://; the core re-classifies, so the rule has one owner. Answered without the index guard (R75) because the remote branch reaches the network

commands.name: sync.status
commands.$comment: §21.13's one command. A read, and idempotent — every sync task is a GET. It is also the sync topic's snapshot, answered through the same handler so the two are one value

commands.name: projects.setReadmeRemote
commands.$comment: §25.5: the per-repository consent for remote README images. NULL is never granted and a timestamp is granted at T, mirroring location.trusted_at. §2.2: a consent change is never auto-replayed. Not folded into projects.setFlags, which §1.2 scopes to the three organisation primitives

commands.name: projects.setFlags
commands.$comment: §2.2: a flag change is non-idempotent and is never auto-replayed. null leaves a flag unchanged

commands.name: projects.setCheckNa
commands.$comment: [p3] §31.6. `na = null` clears the override back to the archetype's proposal; `na = false` is the user OVERRIDING a proposal, so the check is evaluated. N/A is two stored facts and this writes only one of them — a J3 re-run re-proposes and never erases a decision the user made. §2.2: a flag change is never auto-replayed. No new READ command: projects.get and projects.list already serve both surfaces, and a second command for the same fact is a second source of truth.

commands.name: projects.merge
commands.$comment: §11.1: ships with no phase-1 caller and zero call sites outside the test suite

commands.name: projects.unmergeHint
commands.$comment: §1.5: a read-only advisory. It reports what a split would have to decide and decides nothing

commands.name: projects.requeue
commands.$comment: §11.1: re-queues exactly one project's failed and deferred project_job_state rows. TRY AGAIN on one tile means one repository, so this is not scan.start

commands.name: locations.setTrusted
commands.$comment: §1.3/§3.2: writes location.trusted_at in Codotheca's own database, never the user's git config. The -c safe.directory argument is assembled core-side, so no path crosses the wire in either direction

commands.name: locations.relocate
commands.$comment: §17: rewrites path_bytes in place and keeps scan_generation. It is the only phase-1 write to a location's path

commands.name: locations.uninstallPreflight
commands.$comment: §24.7: read-only and UNPRIVILEGED — it writes nothing and originates no path. It does perform a network fetch to verify the remote rather than believe it, so it is not callable on hover

commands.name: locations.uninstall
commands.$comment: §24.8: the verdict is recomputed inside this call and the removal is refused if it changed — a verdict rendered a moment ago is a cache. Non-idempotent: a replay after a core restart would remove a working copy the user has since reinstated

commands.name: targets.setDefault
commands.$comment: §4bis.2a: all three NULL is the global default, the drawer's ANY row. A scope's default is its lowest sort_index; there is no is_default column

commands.name: targets.upsert
commands.$comment: privileged: the executable originates from a shell-owned native dialog. argv is stored and spawned core-side, never through a shell

commands.name: targets.verify
commands.$comment: §4bis.2a: per row and language-blind. Resolution never consults verify_state

commands.name: art.rerender
commands.$comment: §7.4: the absolute target reroll_offset, never an increment, never more than 1 from the stored value, one project per call

commands.name: identity.confirm
commands.$comment: §1.4: apply:false runs the join, returns the delta and writes nothing

commands.name: collections.remove
commands.$comment: §8.8: deletes the collection and collection_member rows and touches nothing else

commands.name: session.focus
commands.$comment: §9: app focus extends a segment only while the focused view is that project, so the renderer must report which project's view holds focus; null means none. §2.4's table omits it. Not privileged — it originates no path and no executable

commands.name: accounts.list
commands.$comment: §20.8: an array, so the renderer handles 0, 1 and more than 1 and never indexes [0] unguarded

commands.name: accounts.orgs
commands.$comment: §20.4: nullable because an org list nobody could enumerate is unknown, and [] would claim there are none

commands.name: accounts.connectPat
commands.$comment: §20.2: the token crosses the wire exactly once, inbound, and is never returned by any command

commands.name: remote.webUrl
commands.$comment: §25.2: NULL when remote_key is NULL, when it is not <host>/<owner>/<name>, or when its host is not allowlisted. Not privileged — it carries no Bytes — and the shell is its only caller: the answer is opened, and only the main process may open it.

commands.name: install.preview
commands.$comment: §24.3a: the renderer names the destination by RootId and the composed display form comes back here, so it never builds one itself. Read-only and unprivileged — it spawns no process and writes nothing, which is what lets the page ask before the user has committed to anything.

commands.name: install.start
commands.$comment: §24.8: privileged because it mutates the filesystem, NOT because it carries Bytes — it carries none (§24.3a), and the destination is a RootId plus the project's stored seed_basename. Non-idempotent: a replay after a core restart begins a second clone into a destination the first is still writing.

commands.name: install.cancel
commands.$comment: §24.3c: kills the clone's process group and removes the staging directory under §24.6's warrant, so it writes to disk as surely as the start did. Non-idempotent: a replay would kill a group a later run may by then own.

commands.name: health.weathering
commands.$comment: [p3] §33.8, and the first name spent from the `health.*` prefix §30 opened and occupied none of (§30.11). It reads `art_scene.scene_json` and nothing else — no debt table, no `health_delta`, no `location`, no clock — so it is read-only and idempotent, and unprivileged because it carries no Bytes and writes nothing. The anchor set is keyed by `scene_hash`, which is why it is a command of its own rather than a field on `ProjectDetail`: that payload is re-fetched on every debt change, and the geometry moves only when the art re-renders.
